title: Local strictly perfect models of tilde of a bounded projective complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], and $P^\bullet$ a complex of $A$-modules, zero outside some finite interval, whose terms are finite and projective (equivalently retracts of finite free modules). For every $x\in Y$ there is an open $U\ni x$ and a strictly perfect complex $K$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex] on the localized site such that the derived restriction of $Q(\widetilde P)$ to $U$ is isomorphic to $Q(K)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. The statement concerns only a complex and restriction, with no arbitrary derived object or perfectness hypothesis.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma perfect-lemma-perfect-affine (Tag 08EB), with More on Algebra, Definition 0656 (a perfect object of D(A) is one isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules)

proof.text: Choose U = top and construct K by applying tilde termwise to P, then applying SheafOfModules.overFunctor termwise. Functor.map_isZero twice preserves the original bounds; K is an explicit complex, not a witness selected from an unproved existence theorem.

For each degree use Mathlib Module.Finite.exists_comp_eq_id_of_projective to obtain f:A^m -> P^n and g:P^n -> A^m with f composed with g equal to the identity. Reindex Pi.basisFun along Equiv.ulift.symm to identify A^m with finitely supported functions on ULift(Fin m). Map this isomorphism by tilde and restriction, use tildeFinsupp and SheafOfModules.mapFreeIso to identify the result with the finite free sheaf. Map g and f and compose with that isomorphism; functoriality and the split equation prove the retract equation.

Use (SheafOfModules.overFunctor R top).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.app on the explicitly constructed tilde complex for the required derived-object isomorphism. Top contains every point, completing the original local statement without any split-off theorem.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08EB reverse implication; second reader completed the termwise retract and derived restriction construction using Mathlib
